sections.content: When a text talks about how history itself gets written — who wrote a source, who compiled it, who promoted an interpretation — passive voice keeps the focus on the source or the idea, with por naming the author only when it matters. These sentences are taken directly from the previous reading.

items.spanish: Casi todos los relatos escritos sobre la conquista fueron redactados por el bando vencedor.
items.english: Almost all the written accounts of the conquest were written by the winning side.

items.spanish: Los pocos testimonios indígenas que sobrevivieron fueron recopilados y traducidos siglos después por Miguel León-Portilla.
items.english: The few indigenous testimonies that survived were compiled and translated centuries later by Miguel León-Portilla.

items.spanish: Durante mucho tiempo fue promovida, sobre todo en España, una interpretación conocida como 'leyenda blanca'.
items.english: For a long time, an interpretation known as the 'white legend' was promoted, especially in Spain.

items.spanish: Ambas leyendas fueron construidas, en última instancia, con fines políticos más que históricos.
items.english: Both legends were built, ultimately, for political rather than historical purposes.

sections.content: Notice that none of these sentences needs a por phrase to make sense — 'leyenda blanca' fue promovida works fine without saying by whom, because the point is that it existed and shaped opinion, not exactly who pushed it hardest. Passive voice lets you make that choice sentence by sentence.
